## 1. Project Overview

DriverSafe is a browser-based driver attention monitoring prototype. The React dashboard requests camera access in the userâ€™s browser, runs MediaPipe Face Landmarker locally to derive 20 normalized facial features, and sends those features over a WebSocket to a FastAPI service. The service applies a NumPy autoencoder, Isolation Forest, and Local Outlier Factor ensemble, adds temporal eye-closure/yawn rules, logs rising-edge drowsiness episodes, and returns per-frame status. Separate HTTP endpoints serve offline model metrics, dataset PCA/clustering, live-session clusters, alert history, export, and simple authentication.

**Stack:** React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Wouter + TanStack Query + Recharts + Tailwind/shadcn-style Radix UI; Python 3.12 + FastAPI + NumPy runtime; MediaPipe Tasks Vision in the browser; PyTorch/scikit-learn/pandas/OpenCV in the training environment; pnpm workspace; Vercel frontend and backend projects.

**Deployment/configuration state observed:** Root Vercel config builds the frontend; `frontend/.vercel/project.json` and `backend/.vercel/project.json` identify separate linked projects. Vercel project metadata in this checkout points at `driversafe` (frontend) and `driversafe-api` (backend). The production frontend hostname is `driversafe.vercel.app`; frontend env names configure a separate HTTPS API host and WSS host. This repository scan does not independently certify current deployment health. Backend Python version is pinned to 3.12. Local API defaults to port 8000 when run with the documented uvicorn command (the root app itself does not launch uvicorn).

**Current state:** Both offline and live inference paths exist. Live feature extraction runs in the browser; trained inference is NumPy-only on the backend. F1 is not computed from the current camera session: it is loaded from `backend/saved_models/results.json`. Live clustering uses a bounded in-process deque of recent valid face features; static metrics and charts use the checked-in synthetic dataset. Auth users, session counters, and WebSocket trackers are process memory, and alert history is a local JSON file.

## 3. Frontend Architecture

### Pages and routing

- **`frontend/src/App.tsx`** â€” wraps the app in TanStack `QueryClientProvider`, Radix `TooltipProvider`, Wouter router, toaster, and a location-keyed error boundary. `/` is a GSAP animated landing page; `/login` and `/signup` render local forms; `/welcome` and `/dashboard/welcome` show `WelcomeSequence`; `/dashboard` is guarded by a token-presence check; unmatched paths render `NotFound`. `ProtectedRoute` checks only `localStorage` token presence, not token validity. Auth submits `login(email,password)` or `signup(name,email,password)`, saves access token, and navigates to `/welcome`.
- **`frontend/src/pages/dashboard.tsx`** â€” single large dashboard containing Live Monitor, Clustering, Metrics, Alert History, and Settings panels. It holds active tab/mobile-nav state and browser session elapsed time. It uses `useDetection` at the dashboard level; live feed stays mounted but is CSS-hidden across tabs. `LiveMonitor` mounts MediaPipe, requests `getUserMedia`, detects landmarks on a 250ms interval, sends `{face_detected,features}` over WebSocket, then charts AE error and displays valid-face count, local alert episode count, static validation F1, model scores/signals. Clustering uses `useClustering` and `useLiveClusters`; metrics uses `useMetrics`; history uses `useAlerts` and CSV export. Profile text/name and sample EAR/MAR/head readout are static presentation values. Camera is browser-only; backend receives feature vectors, not video.
- **`frontend/src/pages/not-found.tsx`** â€” static not-found view with navigation back to `/`.
- **`frontend/src/components/welcome-sequence.tsx`** â€” full-screen scroll/touch/key-controlled welcome transition with external Coverr night-drive video and fallback when video errors. Reduced-motion preference provides a direct enter button. Completing progress navigates to `/dashboard`.

### Components

- **`frontend/src/components/error-boundary.tsx`** â€” class React error boundary with fallback UI and optional `resetKey`; route wrapper resets based on Wouter location.
- **`frontend/src/components/ui/*.tsx`** â€” 55 Radix/shadcn-derived primitives for forms, alerts, controls, navigation, overlay, charts, and status; mostly thin wrappers with `className` and standard Radix props. Dashboard uses several icons/chart primitives directly and does not use every available primitive.
- Dashboard-local components in `dashboard.tsx`: `DashboardPanel`, `AnalyticsStatCard`, `LiveMonitor`, `FeedScore`, `ClusteringPanel`, `MetricsPanel`, `AlertHistory`, `SettingsPanel`, and chart/format helpers. These are not separate component files.
- Landing-local `MagneticLink` and `AuthPage` are defined in `App.tsx`.

### Hooks

- **`frontend/src/hooks/useApi.ts`**: `useMetrics` fetches `/api/metrics/all` once per mount; `useAlerts` fetches alert history + stats and polls every 3 seconds; `useClustering` fetches validation, k-means, PCA once per mount; `useLiveClusters` polls `/api/cluster/live` every second; `useDetection` owns the WebSocket, reconnects after 3 seconds, tracks latest frame/model/signal values and increments browser alert count on falseâ†’true transitions. Its initial threshold is `0.75` until backend data arrives.
- **`use-mobile.tsx`** â€” returns whether viewport is below configured mobile breakpoint via `matchMedia`/resize listener.
- **`use-toast.ts`** â€” local toast store/subscription hook and dispatch helpers used by UI toaster.

### API layer (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts`)

- `BASE_URL = VITE_API_URL || http://localhost:8000`; `WS_URL = VITE_WS_URL || ws://localhost:8000`.
- `login`, `signup`; metrics `getAllMetrics`, `getClusteringMetrics`, `getDetectionMetrics`, `getConfusionMatrix`, `getRocCurve`; alerts `getAlertHistory`, `getAlertStats`, `exportAlerts`; clustering `getKMeans`, `getDBSCAN`, `getPCA`, `getLiveClusters`, `getHierarchical`, `getValidation`; detection `getDetectionStatus`, `getMockFrame`; `DetectionWebSocket` connects to `${WS_URL}/api/detection/ws`.
- `getHeaders()` reads localStorage key `access_token` and sends `Authorization: Bearer â€¦` to HTTP helpers. Backend does not enforce bearer auth on these routes. WebSocket cannot use that helper and sends no authorization token.
- `handleResponse` parses JSON and throws `detail` when present. There is no common retry/timeout policy in this module. WebSocket parses JSON messages, logs parse/errors, closes and reconnects through hook.
- **Contract mismatch:** `signup` sends `{username: email, password, name}` but Pydantic `SignupRequest` accepts only `username` and `password` (default Pydantic extra-field handling ignores the extra name); backend auth calls its field `username` while frontend UI labels it email. Current login/signup uses in-memory backend data.

## 4. Backend Architecture

### FastAPI application (`backend/main.py`)

- `FastAPI(title="DriverSafe API", lifespan=lifespan)`; lifespan invokes `detection.load_models()` once on startup.
- CORS exact origins: `os.getenv("FRONTEND_URL", "https://driversafe.vercel.app")`, `https://driversafe.vercel.app`, `http://localhost:3000`, `http://localhost:5173`, `http://127.0.0.1:5173`; credentials/methods/headers allowed. The env-derived origin may add one further origin.
- Routers: `/api/auth`, `/api/detection`, `/api/cluster`, `/api/metrics`, `/api/alerts`; no custom middleware beyond CORS.
- `GET /` returns `{"status":"DriverSafe API is running"}`; `GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Routers and endpoints

All endpoint details are repeated in Section 6.

- **`backend/routers/auth.py`** â€” `SignupRequest(username min 3, password min 6)`, `LoginRequest(username,password)`, `TokenResponse(access_token,token_type)`. Passwords bcrypt-hashed; JWT `sub` + expiry signed with env `SECRET_KEY` / `ALGORITHM`. User dictionary `fake_users_db` is process memory. `GET /me` returns a constant authenticated response and does not depend on an auth token. Secret fallback at lines 32â€“36 is hardcoded and must not be used in production.
- **`backend/routers/detection.py`** â€” NumPy AE forward pass, compact IF/LOF inference, model loader for `runtime_models.npz`, `autoencoder.npz`, `results.json`; `LiveStreamTracker` maintains eye-closure and yawn state per WebSocket connection. Valid face payload must have `face_detected: true` and exactly 20 list values. Three-model anomaly vote requires at least two of AE error > threshold, IF score < 0, LOF score < 0. Temporal layer sets drowsy when eye closure remains â‰¥1.5 sec, PERCLOS â‰¥80% of â‰¥16 samples in 10 sec, sustained mouth opening â‰¥1.5 sec, at least two recorded yawns within 60 sec, or model consensus. Emits `live_signals`, scores, `votes`, face validity, counts; logs one alert on transition into drowsy. Invalid/missing-face data resets temporal cues, returns zero scores and no alert, and increments total frame count but not valid-face count.
- **`backend/routers/clustering.py`** â€” reads checked-in `full_dataset.csv` at import time for static PCA/KMeans/DBSCAN/hierarchical endpoints. `/live` uses recent in-process valid stream features. NumPy algorithms are in `utils/numpy_ml.py`; runtime scaler/PCA/KMeans compact arrays are loaded from `runtime_models.npz`. If model/data unavailable, it fits locally or generates demonstration points.
- **`backend/routers/metrics.py`** â€” loads `saved_models/results.json` once at import; returns clustering/detection metrics and confusion values. ROC endpoint always serves hardcoded fallback ROC points, even when training results exist. Fallback clustering/confusion/ROC values are in lines 29â€“48.
- **`backend/routers/alerts.py`** â€” returns local JSON history newest-first; returns process-local stats and filtered â€œcurrent sessionâ€ counts; CSV export is plain text from `AlertLogger`.

### Models and utilities

- **`backend/models/autoencoder.py`** â€” PyTorch training/inference class with encoder 20â†’16â†’12â†’8 ReLU and decoder 8â†’12â†’16â†’20; MSE reconstruction error. Training script uses this class; deployed WebSocket router instead has a compatible NumPy layer implementation to avoid PyTorch bundle size.
- **`backend/models/isolation_forest.py`** â€” wrapper around sklearn `IsolationForest`, fit/predict/score helpers.
- **`backend/models/lof.py`** â€” wrapper for sklearn `LocalOutlierFactor(novelty=True)` fit/predict/score helpers.
- **`backend/models/clustering.py`** â€” sklearn scaler/PCA/KMeans/DBSCAN/Agglomerative wrappers and validation/elbow helpers, mainly training/reference code; deployed endpoints use compact NumPy algorithms.
- **`backend/utils/landmark_extractor.py`** â€” legacy/server-side OpenCV + MediaPipe FaceMesh extraction to the 20 training feature order. Not used in live WebSocket route; current live extraction is browser `face-landmarks.ts`.
- **`backend/utils/preprocessor.py`** â€” sklearn StandardScaler/PCA save/load/transform convenience functions for training path.
- **`backend/utils/numpy_ml.py`** â€” compact NumPy scaler/PCA/KMeans/DBSCAN/Agglomerative and clustering score implementations for runtime.
- **`backend/utils/live_session.py`** â€” module-global locked deque (max 300) of feature vectors and process-local counters, session start time, alert frames.
- **`backend/utils/alert_logger.py`** â€” JSON append/read/clear and CSV export. On Vercel filesystem this is not durable/shared unless external persistence is configured.
- `__init__.py` files are package markers; `backend/app.py` re-exports/imports the FastAPI application for alternate entrypoint; `backend/build.py` and Vercel config prepare/limit deployment bundle.

## 5. ML Pipeline

### Dataset and feature schema

CSV directory: `backend/data/landmarks/`. The checked-in `full_dataset.csv` and `test_dataset.csv` each have 1,500 records: 1,000 alert, 300 transition, 200 drowsy. `train_alert.csv` contains 1,000 alert-only rows. All files use synthetic generated observations, not captured/user-labeled driving sessions.

Feature order (20): `left_eye_ear`, `right_eye_ear`, `avg_ear`, `mar`, `left_brow_height`, `right_brow_height`, `head_tilt_x`, `head_tilt_y`, `nose_tip_y`, `left_pupil_x`, `left_pupil_y`, `right_pupil_x`, `right_pupil_y`, `jaw_open`, `left_eye_open`, `right_eye_open`, `mouth_corner_left`, `mouth_corner_right`, `forehead_crease`, `chin_position`. Full/test append `label` (0 alert, 1 transition, 2 drowsy) and `label_name`.

`generate_dataset.py` creates three class-specific distributions with NumPy, clips features to [0,1], writes full/test copies and alert-only training CSV. Training consumes only alert rows for anomaly fit; labels on the full synthetic set are used to score/evaluate.

### Training pipeline (`backend/data/train_models.py`)

1. Read full and alert-only CSVs; use all non-label columns as 20 input features.
2. Fit `StandardScaler` and 10-component PCA on alert training features; save `scaler.pkl`, `pca.pkl`.
3. Train PyTorch AE for 100 epochs with Adam lr 0.001 and MSE; threshold = 95th percentile of alert training errors; save `autoencoder.pt` and runtime `autoencoder.npz` weights.
4. Fit IsolationForest (200 trees, contamination .05, random_state 42); LOF (20 neighbors, contamination .05, novelty=True); save pickle files.
5. Fit KMeans with 3 clusters to alert data; calculate DBSCAN and Ward hierarchical on full set; compute elbow WCSS for k=1..7, silhouette, Daviesâ€“Bouldin.
6. Export fitted scaler, PCA, KMeans, IF tree arrays and LOF state into compact `runtime_models.npz` used by production NumPy inference.
7. Evaluate individual AE/IF/LOF and 2-of-3 ensemble against binary truth `(label == 2)`. Save metrics/confusion/threshold in `results.json`.

|---|---:|---|

### Current saved evaluation (`results.json`)

- Silhouette: **-0.069**; Daviesâ€“Bouldin: **2.266**; WCSS: **18,559.28**; elbow WCSS `[20000.0,19160.76,18559.28,18121.09,17744.72,17423.79,17161.17]`; `optimal_k=3`.
- Ensemble F1 **0.537**, precision **0.367**, recall **1.0**, ROC-AUC **0.867**. Confusion: TP=200, FP=345, FN=0, TN=955. AE threshold **1.483943**.
- Per-model metrics: AE F1 .533 / precision .364 / recall 1 / ROC-AUC .865; IF same; LOF F1 .540 / precision .370 / recall 1 / ROC-AUC .869; ensemble as above.
- â€œROC-AUCâ€ in training is calculated from binary hard predictions (`roc_auc_score(y_true, y_pred)`), not continuous scores; values are not a conventional threshold-swept ROC evaluation. This synthetic validation is not a live-camera F1.

## 7. Data Flow

### Live Monitor

1. `/dashboard` creates `useDetection`; it opens a WebSocket to `VITE_WS_URL + /api/detection/ws` and reconnects on close.
2. Browser requests webcam permission; MediaPipe Tasks Vision loads the face-landmarker model from a remote Google-hosted asset and runs locally every 250ms.
3. `extractFaceFeatures` computes the ordered 20-value vector and clamps it to [0,1]. Browser sends feature list and face flag; raw images/video are not uploaded.
4. Backend validates shape, scales with training mean/scale, calculates AE reconstruction error, IF decision score, LOF score, 2-of-3 model votes, then temporal cues.
5. Backend sends result JSON; hook updates scores, face state, counts, signals. Alert count increments on rising drowsy edge; backend logger writes episode on the same edge.

### Clustering tab

`useClustering` fetches validation/KMeans/PCA once; these endpoints operate over the saved synthetic `full_dataset.csv`. `useLiveClusters` separately polls `/api/cluster/live` each second; it projects and clusters up to the latest 300 valid feature frames in the current backend process. It returns empty until at least three are available. Static clustering plots and live points therefore describe different populations.

### Metrics tab

`useMetrics` fetches `/api/metrics/all` once on mount. It reads the checked-in `results.json`; the F1 card is the offline ensemble result. Confusion comes from saved offline evaluation. ROC comes from fallback hardcoded arrays and does not correspond to `results.json` AUC when real results are present.

### Alerts tab

`useAlerts` polls `/api/alerts/history` and `/api/alerts/stats` every 3 seconds. Backend returns alerts from `backend/data/alerts/alerts.json` (created on startup/write) and in-process counters; export downloads CSV from `/api/alerts/export`. On serverless, files and process globals can reset or differ across instances.

### WebSocket flow

Browser `DetectionWebSocket.connect` â†’ FastAPI accepts â†’ receives text JSON â†’ validates `face_detected` and exactly 20 values â†’ models + tracker â†’ records valid feature/counter â†’ logs alert on state transition â†’ sends result JSON. No-face/malformed frame clears temporal eye/yawn accumulation and emits false drowsy state with zero scores. Each connection owns its own `LiveStreamTracker`, while aggregate counters are per Python process.

## 8. Issues Found

### Critical / functionality risks

1. **Auth is process-local, not durable.** `backend/routers/auth.py:13-14,39-66` stores users in `fake_users_db`. Signup accounts disappear on a cold start, redeploy, or different function instance; a later login may fail. Use a persistent user store if auth is intended to be real.
2. **Signing key has a source-code fallback.** `backend/routers/auth.py:32-36` uses `driversafe_secret_key_2026_rishu` when `SECRET_KEY` is absent. Missing configuration should fail closed with a strong secret rather than sign JWTs with a known literal.
3. **Auth is not enforced.** `backend/routers/auth.py:68-70` `/me` does not inspect a token; all data routes are unprotected. Frontend token gating is only a client-side presence check (`App.tsx` `ProtectedRoute`). The WebSocket sends no token.
4. **Production alert persistence is not durable/shared.** `backend/utils/alert_logger.py` writes local JSON; `backend/routers/detection.py:43` points it at `backend/data/alerts/alerts.json`. Vercel function filesystems and multi-instance functions do not provide shared persistent state. Alert history can vanish or be inconsistent.
5. **Session statistics are process-global, not per user/session.** `backend/utils/live_session.py:8-13` counters/start time live at module import; `record_frame` aggregates multiple connections and Vercel instances independently. `/api/alerts/stats` reports process uptime as the â€œsession,â€ not a browserâ€™s session.
6. **Input feature semantics differ from training.** The live browser and legacy Python extractor derive heuristic landmarks and clamp all values to [0,1], while training data is generated from synthetic class distributions. Scores/thresholds may not be calibrated to actual MediaPipe values, so detections and model votes may be poor even though transport works.

### F1 score (why it is fixed at 0.54)

- UI source: `frontend/src/pages/dashboard.tsx:372` displays `metrics?.detection.f1_score?.toFixed(2)` and explicitly labels it â€œOffline score Â· updates after retrainingâ€.
- Backend source: `backend/routers/metrics.py:14-26,71-82` reads JSON once at module import; endpoint returns stored `detection.f1_score` and never uses current stream labels.
- Saved value: `backend/saved_models/results.json:17-22` stores `"f1_score": 0.537`, rendered as **0.54**.
- Calculation: `backend/data/train_models.py` `evaluate_models()` around the block defining `y_binary = (y_full == 2)`, `ensemble = ((ae_preds + if_preds + lof_preds) >= 2)`, and `f1_score(y_true,y_pred,zero_division=0)`. Truth is synthetic CSV `label == 2`, not human labels for the live feed. `roc_auc_score` also consumes binary predictions, reducing ROC-AUC meaning.
- Effect: live camera changes `ae_error`, IF/LOF scores, votes, cue state and drowsy episodes; it cannot change F1 because no labeled live ground truth or online metric accumulator exists. The constant 0.54 is expected from this implementation, not a UI refresh fault.

### Drowsy detection / alert behavior

- Current live event logic: `backend/routers/detection.py:56-104`; eye features 14/15 below `.48` for â‰¥1.5s OR >=80% of 16+ samples within a rolling 10s; yawn uses feature 3 >=.55 continuously for 1.5s; 2 yawns within a minute or model 2/3 consensus also marks drowsy.
- Alert episode is written only when `result["is_drowsy"]` changes falseâ†’true: `detection.py:281-283`. If features do not satisfy these thresholds, or valid frames arrive too slowly/irregularly, event remains zero. A single visibly open mouth frame is not a sustained yawn. It is appropriate for ordinary awake frames to remain at zero.
- Browser event counter is separately edge-counted in `frontend/src/hooks/useApi.ts` inside the WebSocket message handler. It resets when the page is remounted/reloaded and is not the persisted history count.
- **Feature-index concern:** `LiveStreamTracker` assumes feature 3 (MAR) and 14/15 (eye EAR Ã—2.5). The current browser mapping must remain aligned with this order; clamping eye features to 1 caps them and makes the `.48` closed-eye threshold correspond to unscaled EAR < .192. This is unusually strict relative to common EAR closure thresholds and should be calibrated against observed frames.
- **LOF alert score direction differs between runtime and mock:** real route checks raw decision `< 0` (`detection.py:154-156`); `process_frame_mock()` checks `lof_score > 1.5` (`detection.py:218-230`). Mock output is not a reliable simulation of production model semantics.
- Alert logger field bug: `AlertLogger.log_alert()` stores `scores.get("lof",0)` (`backend/utils/alert_logger.py`), but live result names that score `lof_score`; saved alert history therefore records LOF as zero. It stores model cue names, not the nested `model_alerts` dictionary.
- Drowsy count `/api/alerts/stats` only includes JSON records after process-global import timestamp and checks logged state; yawn count expects state `YAWN` although live logger writes only `DROWSY`. This makes `yawn_alerts` stay zero even if yawns contribute to a DROWSY episode.

### Other bugs / mismatches

- `backend/routers/detection.py:253` returns hardcoded `ws://localhost:8000/...` even in production. Current frontend correctly builds its WebSocket URL from `VITE_WS_URL`, but status consumers could use the wrong URL.
- `backend/routers/metrics.py:98-101`: ROC is fixed fallback (`auc:0.91`) rather than the saved `0.867`; graph and endpoint AUC can disagree with actual saved evaluation.
- `backend/routers/clustering.py`: static clustering is over the synthetic labeled dataset; live clustering is separate and requires 3 frames. UI naming must avoid implying the static clusters are current driver observations.
- `backend/routers/clustering.py` `_scaled()` standardizes with saved scaler if present; fallback computes mean/std over each requestâ€™s input (so points can shift as live window changes). Live API includes every valid frame up to 300 and no session/user key.
- `backend/routers/auth.py` requires password min length 6, while frontend form requires min 8; not fatal but inconsistent. `SignupRequest` ignores frontend `name` and no profile is returned.
- `backend/utils/landmark_extractor.py` is unused in active browser path but adds OpenCV/MediaPipe requirements to training/legacy requirements and uses a different MediaPipe API path than browser Tasks Vision.
- API OpenAPI spec only declares `/healthz`, which FastAPI does not expose (`/health` instead). Generated clients are not a complete/current contract.
- UI contains hardcoded profile â€œRishu Sharmaâ€, session code DS-INT396, EAR/MAR sample readout and webcam badge â€œ4 FPSâ€; FPS is not measured.
- Default dashboard F1 fallback displays `N/A` only while query is unavailable; errors are stored in hook but dashboard mostly does not render query errors.
- No direct test suite is listed in repository manifests/tree. Type/build commands exist but were not run as part of this read-only architecture scan.

## 11. Incomplete / Known Limitations

- âŒ Live F1 is not implemented; the displayed value is offline synthetic validation.
- âŒ Static clustering/metrics are not calculated from the live camera; only `/cluster/live` projects current process-buffered feature vectors.
- âŒ Alert history, users and session counters are not durable or shared between serverless instances.
- âŒ Auth is not robust: in-memory accounts, known signing fallback, incomplete token validation/enforcement.
- âŒ ROC points are hardcoded and may disagree with reported offline AUC.
- âŒ Live ML calibration against real labeled camera data is not evidenced; current model was trained on synthetic features.
- âŒ OpenAPI document omits almost all actual endpoints and declares health path mismatch.
- âŒ Live alert log stores zero LOF score due `lof` vs `lof_score` key mismatch; separate yawn count is not populated by current DROWSY logger.

## 12. Improvements Needed

### Priority 1 â€” reliability and validity

1. Calibrate and validate extraction against real, consented labeled samples; align browser/Python/training feature distributions and eye/yawn thresholds. Keep live event count distinct from offline metrics.
2. Replace process-local fake users with persistent auth storage; remove hardcoded JWT secret fallback; validate JWT and protect HTTP/WebSocket routes; send token on WebSocket securely.
3. Persist alert/session data in a real shared database/store before relying on Vercel serverless history or cross-instance counters.
4. Correct `lof_score` alert serialization, define whether yawn is its own event or a DROWSY reason, and test edge detection/reset behavior.

### Priority 2 â€” trustworthy analytics and API contract

1. Calculate ROC-AUC from continuous anomaly scores and show training dataset/version, precision/recall/confusion alongside F1; do not represent offline F1 as live.
2. Generate ROC points from saved evaluation data; remove hardcoded metrics fallback from production or clearly flag demo values.
3. Version and complete OpenAPI contract for actual endpoints and align `/health` versus `/healthz`.
4. Scope live clustering data by session/user, expose sample count/time range, and distinguish synthetic/static plots.
5. Render network/loading/error states for panels and remove hardcoded profile/metric readout/FPS.

### Priority 3 â€” maintenance

1. Split `dashboard.tsx` into smaller tab/component files; centralize runtime schemas/types for HTTP and WebSocket payloads.
2. Add automated tests for feature ordering, no-face behavior, duration thresholds, model scores, endpoints and frontend/backend contracts.
3. Keep legacy server-side FaceMesh/OpenCV extractor only if it is deliberately supported; otherwise document it as training/utility code.
4. Regenerate TypeScript API/Zod clients only after API spec is made authoritative.

## 14. Environment & Deployment

- **Frontend:** Vercel root project builds the Vite app from `frontend/`; package build is `vite build --config vite.config.ts`; workspace/root build runs typecheck then package builds. `frontend/vercel.json` and root `vercel.json` configure SPA output/rewrites. Production URL `https://driversafe.vercel.app`. Runtime build variables: `VITE_API_URL`, `VITE_WS_URL`; exact values redacted.
- **Backend:** separate Vercel Python project, source root `backend`, app entry `main:app`/`app.py` compatibility. `backend/.python-version` is `3.12`; deployment config includes compact model files and function duration configuration. Local typical command is `cd backend; uvicorn main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`; the application source does not call `uvicorn.run` itself. For Vercel production state, repository metadata shows separate API project; current live health was not probed during this document generation.
- **Local configuration:** `.env.example` lists expected backend names; `.env` and Vercel local metadata contain sensitive values and are intentionally redacted. Vercel secrets are configured externally and cannot be established from committed code.
- **Deployment status caveat:** source/configuration establishes intended deployment targets but current serving health, deployment commit, and Vercel environment values need a live service check or Vercel dashboard inspection to confirm. A source scan alone cannot prove availability.

### Backend

- Runtime `requirements.txt`: FastAPI â‰¥0.111, Uvicorn standard â‰¥0.29, python-jose crypto â‰¥3.3, passlib bcrypt â‰¥1.7.4, bcrypt `<4.1.0`, python-dotenv â‰¥1.0, NumPy `>=1.26,<2.0`, Pydantic â‰¥2.
- Training/legacy `requirements-training.txt` includes runtime requirements plus pandas â‰¥2.2, scikit-learn `==1.9.0`, joblib â‰¥1.3, PyTorch CPU `==2.2.2+cpu`, MediaPipe `==0.10.21`, and headless OpenCV â‰¥4.9.
- **Python compatibility:** selected deployment runtime is Python 3.12. Python 3.14 compatibility is not asserted or tested by repository metadata. PyTorch, MediaPipe, NumPy/scikit-learn binary wheels are version/platform-sensitive; use the pinned 3.12 deployment/training environment unless those packages are separately verified on 3.14. Minimal runtime avoids importing the heavier training stack for live inference, although `landmark_extractor.py` belongs to legacy utility code.
- **Potential concern:** scikit-learn is exactly pinned at 1.9.0 in training requirements while runtime pickle artifacts depend on sklearn serialization compatibility. Training and artifact generation should use the same pinned environment as the artifacts were created with.
